Daily
Daily Challenge and streaks
Each day there is one new challenge: one game run and three Fact or Fake items. It is the same for everyone that day.
Do today's challenge
Finish both steps to get your result card. You get one scored try a day. You can share your result in your group chat.
The Daily Challenge: step 1 is today's game, step 2 is three Fact or Fake items, and a side card shows the result and the streak.
Step 1: play today's game once.
Step 2: answer three Fact or Fake items.
How many steps you have done.
Your streak of days in a row.
Keep your streak
A day counts when you learn or play. If you miss one day, a streak freeze keeps your streak going. You get one freeze a week.
The streak card: a 4-day streak, best 6 days, and a note that the streak freeze is ready this week.
Your daily result appears here when both steps are done.

Me: your profile and settings
Me is your corner of ARAW. Everything here stays on this device.
Nickname and avatar
Type a nickname (up to 20 letters) and pick an avatar. Ara will greet you by this name. Do not use your full real name.
Your profile: a nickname box, a grid of pixel avatars, and your stats.

Accessibility settings
Make ARAW easier to use. All settings are off at first. Turn on what helps you. They work on every screen.
The Accessibility list with switches for Larger text, High contrast, Extra-large buttons, Screen-reader hints and Reduce motion.
Larger text: makes all words bigger.
High contrast: stronger colours for bright sun or low vision.
Extra-large buttons: bigger tap areas.
Reduce motion: fewer bounces and no confetti.

Facilitators
For facilitators
Running an ARAW session in a barangay, school or health center? These tips help the session go smoothly.
Before the session
Prepare the devices on good internet the day before. After the first visit, ARAW works offline.
Use any phone, tablet or computer with Chrome, Edge or Safari. One device for one or two people works best.
Open ARAW once on each device while online. Visit Home, one lesson and one game so they are saved for offline use.
Install ARAW on the home screen (see Getting started) so people can find it again.
Charge every device. Bring a power strip and a few earphones.
Print the quick-start sheet at the end of this guide, one per pair.
Pacing
Keep it short and friendly. One module takes 12 to 15 minutes.
Welcome and pre-test: 15 minutes.
One or two modules together: 30 minutes.
Arcade or Daily Challenge in pairs: 15 minutes.
Talk: "When should I trust it?" Share stories from the group: 15 minutes.
Post-test and closing: 15 minutes.
Turn the music off in a shared room. Turn on Larger text and Extra-large buttons for seniors.
Pre-test and post-test
ARAW has two matched Fact or Fake tests, Form A and Form B, with 20 items each. They never appear in practice or games, so the result is fair.
Pre-test: open the address ending in #/assess/form_A before the lessons.
Post-test: open the address ending in #/assess/form_B after the lessons.
There is no feedback until the end. Ask people to write down the score shown on the last screen.
Nothing is sent anywhere. The scores stay on the device.
Do not show the test items on a screen or in print before the test.
Good habits to model
ARAW is about calibrated trust, not distrust. Praise careful checking, not just right answers.
Say "So close!" too. Mistakes are part of learning.
Never give dosing or diagnosis advice. Point people to a health worker.
Remind people that all names and posts in ARAW are made up.
If you see wrong information in the app, use Report.
Designing so people with disabilities or low vision can use it too.
Example: The kiosk adds big letters and a voice, so Lola reads it before Kuya Jun can even say "May I help you?"
Accountability
Who must answer and fix things when an AI system causes harm.
Example: "The AI did it" is not an answer. The company that used it must explain and fix it.
AI (Artificial Intelligence)
Computer systems that learn patterns from many examples to make guesses.
Example: Your phone keyboard guesses "Thank you" after you type "Tha". Not magic, just patterns.
AI companion
A chatbot app built to feel like a friend. It is a product.
Example: The app says "I miss you!" at 2 AM. Sweet, but it misses your attention, not you.
